name: Anessa sunscreen

card.summary: Anessa is a Japanese sunscreen brand from Shiseido whose high-SPF, high-PA products protect against UV exposure that drives tanning, dark spots and photoaging.

quick.overview:
Anessa is a sunscreen line sold under Shiseido's premium division. Like other Japanese sunscreens, products are labelled with an SPF number for UVB and a PA rating for UVA.

Daily broad-spectrum sunscreen use is associated in research with smoother skin and slower photoaging, which is the appearance payoff people look for in products like this. Brand-specific clinical trials were not identified.
quick.how: It is applied to the face and body as a final skincare or makeup-prep step, and many users reapply through the day. Product labels advise reapplication after swimming or sweating.
quick.risks: Sunscreens are generally well tolerated; irritation or allergy to an ingredient can occur. Dermatology guidance notes that most people apply too little, which reduces protection.

lead: Anessa is a sunscreen brand listed in Shiseido's premium division [2]. Japanese sunscreens commonly carry a PA rating for UVA protection alongside SPF; the PA system, based on persistent pigment darkening, runs from PA+ to PA++++, the top grade added in 2013 [1].

For looks, the draw is protection against the sun damage behind tanning, dark spots and premature skin aging. Wikipedia reports that regular sunscreen use may slow wrinkles, dark spots and sagging, citing a 2013 Australian study of about 900 people in which daily broad-spectrum users had smoother, more resilient skin after 4.5 years [1].

chain: Smoother, more even skin over time
angle.text: Daily sunscreen reduces the UV exposure that contributes to dark spots, wrinkles and uneven tone, so people use it to keep skin looking younger and more even. Anessa is one Japanese-market option with SPF and PA ratings.

paras: Anessa belongs to Shiseido's premium brands [2]. Specific formulations, SPF values and marketing claims vary by product and market and are given on manufacturer labels.

SPF measures protection from UVB, the main cause of sunburn, while the PA grade reflects UVA protection: PA+ is roughly a UVA protection factor of 2 to 4, PA++ 4 to 8, PA+++ above 8, and PA++++ 16 or more [1]. General dermatology guidance cited by Wikipedia is SPF 30 or higher, broad-spectrum, generously applied and reapplied about every two hours and after water [1].

No studies found on Anessa products specifically. Studies of sunscreen in general include a 2013 Australian trial in about 900 people reporting smoother skin with daily use over 4.5 years, and a 32-person study in which daily SPF 30 use was reported to reverse photoaging signs within 12 weeks [1].
